sentences.text:
The brief facts of the case are as under:
Upon a complaint lodged by Mallesh Gudadappa Talakal, Hubli Rural Police registered a case in Crime No. 0214/2020 for the offence punishable under section 498A, 302, 304B and 201 read with Section 34 IPC, wherein, the present petitioner is shown as Accused No.4.
4.
The complaint averments reveal that Netravathi being the daughter of the complainant, studied BE in Hubli and after completion of her studies, she joined a private company in Hospet.
After some time, with all earnings and belongings, she left her parents and started living in the house of Ramachandrappa Neelakantappa Kale at Shiraguppi.
The complainant and his family members severed all connections with the Netravathi and decided that Netravathi is no longer concerned to their family.
Thereafterwords, they came to know that Netravathi is NC: 2023:KHC-D:7416 getting married to Ramachandrappa Neelakantappa Kale.
Complainant and his family members did not attend the marriage.

Subsequent to the marriage, two - three times, Netravathi called her mother i.e., the wife of the complainant stating that there is a physical and mental harassment imparted to her on the ground of demand of dowry including the present petitioner.

However, the wife of the complainant did not bring it to the notice of the police about the said harassment, but she told that she has married against the will of the members of the family of the complainant and therefore, she has to suffer the same.

Subsequently, on 07.11.2020 at about 9.00 a.m., when the complainant was in his house, he received call from Suresh who is the brother-in-law that Netravathi died in the Ramachandrappa Neelakantappa Kale's house.
Accordingly, the complainant and his wife and others visited the house of Ramachandrappa Neelakantappa Kale at Shiraguppi and noticed that the dead body had a ligature mark around the neck.

Thereafter, they lodged a complaint before the police that accused persons including NC: 2023:KHC-D:7416 the present petitioner, harassed Nethravathi for want of dowry and ultimately, killed her and in order to escape from the rigors of law, they made it appear that she committed suicide and therefore, sought for action.
Police after registering the case, based on the said complaint, registered a case as aforesaid and are investigating the matter and filed the charge sheet.
5. Petitioner is the 4th accused in the said charge sheet.
6. Learned Magistrate has taken cognizance and the matter is now in the process of committing to the Sessions Court for trial.

Registering the case against the petitioner has been challenged by the 4th accused on the following grounds:
 "It is submitted that in the first instance, it is made clear that no such incidence is occurred as alleged by the complainant.
It is a false complaint Just to harass the petitioners and to see them behind the bars.
This is the classic case for abuse of process of law.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:7416  It is submitted that there are no ingredients of the offence made out in the complaint so as to attract the same.

At a glance of the complaint, it can be easily made out that, at the instance of complainant, Complaint came to be Lalita D/O Nilakantappa Chalawadi ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131122508/
3 registered to see the petitioner behind the bars.

sentences.text: It is submitted that complainant has filed a false Complaint against all family members.
It is submitted that there is nothing in the complaint to attract the ingredients of the offences punishable Under sec. 498A, 306, 304B, 201 R/w. Sec.34 of IPC and Sec.3 of D.P. Act.
That petitioner is residing her matrimonial House at Kooliwad Village along with her husband and two children.

The petitioners hailing from a religious and humble family, and more specifically from a priestly class which generally engages in performing all the religious and pious functions have never imagined the committing any offence against anybody.
It is submitted that the post mortem report clearly demonstrates that the death is not due to homicidal hanging.
The witnesses relied by the prosecution are merely hearsay witnesses and hence there is no material evidence against the accused/petitioner.
If the charge sheet is allowed to sustain it will seriously prejudice the rights of the petitioners as it would only amount to an abuse of process of law by the complainant.
It is submit that, after carefully evaluating the materials on record, it does not disclose the involvement of the above petitioner/Accused No. 4 in the said case.
But the IO falsely implicated the innocent petitioner/Accused No.4 as accused in the above case.

It is submitted that in the same set facts this Hon'ble Court has quashed the proceedings against the co-accused i.e. accused No.5 who is the sister of the present petitioner in Crl.P. No.101644/2021 on 07/06/2022 by this Hon'ble Court.
 That if the impugned proceedings are allowed to be continued it would certainly amount to an abuse of process of court and as such proceedings should be quashed at this stage itself.

The petitioners may be allowed to urge additional grounds at the time of hearing."
NC: 2023:KHC-D:7416 7.

Reiterating the above grounds, the learned counsel for the petitioner Shri. S. B. Doddagoudar,
contended that the present petitioner is living at Koliwad and she is the sister-in-law of the Lalita D/O Nilakantappa Chalawadi ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131122508/
4 complainant and since she has not share any common roof along with the other accused persons,
pending criminal proceedings against the present petitioner needs to be quashed.
8.

entities.text: Lalita D/O Nilakantappa Chalawadi ... vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He also brought to the notice of the Court that in respect of accused No.5 this Court already quashed the pending criminal proceedings by passing the order dated 07.06.2022 in Criminal Petition No.101644/2021 and sought for quashing of the proceedings in respect of accused No.4.
9.
Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader contended that there are allegations of overt acts insofar as the present petitioner is concerned and sought for dismissal of the petition.

10. Perused the material on record in the light of the rival contention of the parties.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:7416 11.
On such perusal of the material on record, it is noticed that the present petitioner has not shared common roof along with the other accused persons.
Similarly placed accused No.5 had already approached this Court and the pending criminal proceedings was quashed insofar as accused No.5 is concerned.
12. The allegations found against the present petitioner and accused No.5 are practically similar.

Therefore, a case is made out for interference in quashing the pending criminal proceedings against the petitioner/accused No.4 by exercising the power vested in this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
13.
Accordingly, the following order is passed.

ORDER (i) The Criminal Petition is allowed.
(ii) Consequently, the entire proceedings pending before the JMFC II Court, Hubballi in C.C.
No.173/2021 for the offences punishable - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7416 under Sections 498A, 306, 304B, 201 read with section 34 of IPC and Section 3 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, insofar as the petitioner/accused No.4 is concerned is hereby quashed.
Ordered accordingly.
Sd/-
